transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

I’m here because I feel like something’s not right about what happened around my father’s death. People keep telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all match up, but when I look at the timestamps, missing attachments, and how certain people in the community avoid answering my questions, it just seems obvious to me that someone is hiding the truth.
How long have you been having these thoughts and concerns about your father's death being covered up?
About nine months. It started after my father died, when I was going through his records and messages, and I started noticing things that didn’t add up.
Since these concerns started nine months ago, have you also been feeling persistently sad, low, or lost interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t know that I’d call it persistently sad. I’ve been stressed and preoccupied with all of this, but I haven’t really thought about it in terms of losing interest in things.
Have you had any recent medical issues, head injuries, or new medications/substance use, or noticed any changes in your memory or thinking clarity around the time these concerns started?

I don’t think so. I haven’t had a head injury or anything like that, and I’m not aware of any medical issue that started around then. My memory and thinking seem clear to me. I’d have to think about medications or substances, but nothing stands out as new around that time.
Have you noticed any new physical symptoms like headaches, dizziness, seizures, vision changes, or times when your alertness or consciousness seemed to fluctuate since this all started?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. No seizures or vision changes, and I don’t think my alertness has been changing. I’ve felt stressed, but physically I don’t think there’s been anything new.
Aside from this concern about your father's death, how are things going in other areas of your life—like work, relationships, and daily routine?

Mostly okay, I guess. I still go to work and keep up with my projects. I pay my bills, do my usual routine, that kind of thing. It’s not like everything has fallen apart.

The main issue is when I bring up my questions about my father’s records. That’s when things can get tense with family, or sometimes people in the community. Otherwise, day to day, I’m functioning pretty normally.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a single, well-systematized, non-bizarre delusional belief (that his father's death was covered up, based on his interpretation of records, timestamps, and community avoidance) persisting for approximately 9 months. There are no hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or other features of broader psychotic disorganization. Mood symptoms (persistent sadness, anhedonia) were explicitly denied, ruling out a mood disorder with psychotic features. Organic causes (head injury, medical illness, substance use, fluctuating consciousness) were screened and denied. Aside from the specific delusional theme, the patient maintains normal occupational and daily functioning, which is characteristic of delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia (which typically involves broader functional decline and additional psychotic symptoms) or brief psychotic disorder (duration criterion not met, as symptoms have persisted beyond 1 month, in fact 9 months, arguing against brief psychotic disorder but consistent with delusional disorder's chronicity).
